collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — HEALING, PSYCHOLOGY AND MEDICINE (HEA-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Healers, herbs, teas, poultices, mushrooms, potions, island magic, listening, breathing, routines and rest. Care for the body and care for the mind, with every kind of healing treated with equal respect. Treatments can help, help a little, do nothing or have side effects. Nobody has to be cured, nobody is mocked, and the villager always decides.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult and a healer, elder or spiritual leader)

collection.description: A villager who has felt grey for weeks sits beside a friend under a tree: say how it has been, or talk of other things.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: For weeks now, (subject) has felt flat. Not sad exactly. Grey. Food tastes of nothing much, jokes don't land, and getting up in the morning feels like lifting a canoe. (subject.He/she) hasn't told anyone. Today (subject.he/she) finds (friend) sitting alone under the big breadfruit tree and, before (subject.he/she) can stop (subject.him/her)self, sits down too.

text_only.reason: food in the story (a meal, a catch, fruit); the village's stores do not change -- the draft's notes: everything but the marked effects is story only

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "I don't know what's wrong," says (subject). "Nothing's happened. I just feel grey." (friend) doesn't tell (subject.him/her) to cheer up. (friend.He/she) asks how (subject) is sleeping, what (subject.he/she) still enjoys, even a little. They talk until the shadows move. "Come back next week," says (friend). "Same tree. We'll talk again." (subject) does. Some weeks are a little lighter. Some aren't. (subject.He/she) keeps coming to the tree.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) can't quite say it. Instead they talk about fishing, and the weather, and a goat that keeps getting onto the storehouse roof. (friend) seems to understand something anyway. "I'm under this tree most afternoons," (friend.he/she) says as (subject) gets up. "If you ever want to talk about something that isn't goats." (subject) nods. (subject.He/she) isn't ready yet. (subject.He/she) knows where the tree is.
